how_it_works: Martial arts is a specialization of brawling (brawling: martial arts); some gamemasters keep it loose.
For every full 1D the martial arts skill increases, the character picks one technique. Increases of one or two pips do not count. Raising the skill during character creation counts.
A technique must be declared before making the required skill roll (unless noted).
Most techniques only work if the attack succeeds and is not parried or dodged and the skill roll meets the technique's difficulty.
example: Skill 3D+2 raised to 5D+2 at creation = two techniques. Later 5D+2 -> 6D gives none (only +1 pip); the next technique comes at 6D+2.

techniques.name: Blindfighting
techniques.effect: Within striking distance, ignore the effects of blindness (hear or smell the target). May be used as a reaction skill.

techniques.name: Disarm
techniques.effect: On a successful, unparried attack, the target is disarmed.

techniques.name: Elbow Smash
techniques.effect: +1D to damage on a successful skill roll.

techniques.name: Flip
techniques.effect: Throws a target who grappled you from behind to the ground (not parried or dodged); 3D damage. May be used as a reaction skill.

techniques.name: Flying Kick
techniques.effect: +2D damage if the roll exceeds the difficulty; on failure the character is off balance and the opponent gets an extra attack this round with no multiple-action penalty.

techniques.name: Foot Sweep
techniques.effect: Target is tripped and falls. As printed: the character must remain prone for the rest of the round (see errata).

techniques.name: Head-Butt
techniques.effect: Strike with the head for STR+1D damage, even when held, pinned or bound. May be used as a reaction skill.

techniques.name: Hold/Grapple
techniques.difficulty: Moderate plus Strength versus martial arts
techniques.effect: Moderate martial arts roll to hold; each round held, the holder rolls Strength or lifting. The target breaks free by beating the holder's martial arts (or Strength/lifting) roll.

techniques.name: Instant Knockdown
techniques.effect: Target is knocked down; the fallen character waits a round to stand or suffers multiple-action penalties.

techniques.name: Instant Stand
techniques.effect: Return to standing after being tripped or knocked down without a multiple-action penalty.

techniques.name: Instant Stun
techniques.effect: Target is stunned for one round.

techniques.name: Instant Wound
techniques.effect: Target suffers a wound (effects cumulative).

techniques.name: Multiple Strikes
techniques.effect: A second attack with no multiple-action penalty; it inflicts 3D damage.

techniques.name: Nerve Punch
techniques.effect: A named arm or leg is unusable for 3D rounds and held items are dropped; beating the difficulty by 15+ knocks the target unconscious.

techniques.name: Power Block
techniques.effect: A successful parry inflicts STR+1D on the attacker. May be used as a reaction skill.

techniques.name: Reversal
techniques.difficulty: Opposed Strength or brawling: martial arts (higher)
techniques.effect: Only when held. Breaking the grip lets the character hold the opponent or use another technique. May be used as a reaction skill.

techniques.name: Silent Strike
techniques.effect: After successfully sneaking up (within arm's reach), kill or knock out the target; declare which beforehand.

techniques.name: Spinning Kick
techniques.effect: +1D damage if the roll exceeds the difficulty; on failure off balance and the opponent gets an extra attack this round with no penalty.

techniques.name: Shoulder Throw
techniques.effect: Target hurled to the ground (not parried or dodged) for 3D damage.

techniques.name: Weapon Block
techniques.difficulty: Opposed martial arts versus melee combat
techniques.effect: Parry melee attacks without holding a melee weapon.

options_for_gamemasters: Basic moves only first: punch (STR+1D), kick (STR+2D), weapon block (opposed martial arts vs melee combat).
Character Points cannot be used on martial arts rolls (Force Points can).
Style packages: the gamemaster limits available techniques; learning one outside the style costs 10 Character Points and three weeks.
Parrying: martial arts can be used to both parry and attack, but brawling parry cannot be used for a brawling attack.
Untrained: Grapple/Hold without the specialization is +2 difficulty levels; with the specialization but without the technique, +1 level. Some techniques (Silent Strike) cannot be done untrained.
